# Research: Privacy Protection (Spec 023)

**Date**: 2026-10-11 · **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

Tags: **[V]** verified from the source (license file, `javap` of `androidx.webkit` 1.17.0 `classes.jar` and its `-sources.jar`, measured list files); **[D]** framework documentation; **[B]** belief, to confirm on a device during the gates.

---

## R1 — Tracker list source and license

**Decision**: Ship a **host-level subset of EasyPrivacy + EasyList**, taken under their **CC BY-SA 3.0** licence option, generated by a script in the repo and committed as an asset. Measured with the planned filter: **≈15,900 hosts, ≈108 KB gzip** [V].

**Rationale**
- EasyList and EasyPrivacy are dual-licensed **GPLv3+ or CC BY-SA 3.0+**, at the user's option [V, easylist.to/pages/licence.html]. Under the CC option, ShareAlike binds the *derived list*, not the app's code; bundling a data file beside code is a collection [assumption — standard CC 3.0 reading]. Attribution: "The EasyList authors (https://easylist.to/)".
- The scope the owner chose in clarification (trackers + ad networks, not content embeds) matches EasyPrivacy (trackers) + EasyList's ad-server hosts (ad networks). None of youtube.com, googlevideo.com, ytimg.com, accounts.google.com, appleid.apple.com, maps.googleapis.com, gstatic.com, fonts.googleapis.com or the major CDNs appear in the extraction [V]. FR-004a is still enforced in code with a small hand-written **never-block** set (R3).
- Coverage yardstick (DuckDuckGo's 346 block-by-default, non-content trackers, used only for measuring, not shipped): EasyPrivacy+EasyList hosts cover **251/346** [V].

**Generation rules** (script `tools/protection-lists/build_tracker_hosts.py`, run by hand when the list is refreshed; never run by Gradle, never at runtime):
- keep `||host^` rules, with or without request-type options;
- drop rules with `domain=`, `popup`, a path, `@@` exceptions, cosmetic rules, the CNAME-uncloaking and adult sections;
- reduce EasyList ad-server hosts to keep the file within the R9 budget (the measured 15.9k set used a popularity trim; if the trim source's licence does not allow use, fall back to EasyList's `easylist_adservers` section only and re-measure — the budget, not the trim method, is the requirement);
- write `assets/protection/tracker_hosts.txt` with a header naming the sources, the date, the licence and "modified: host-level subset".

**Alternatives rejected**
- **DuckDuckGo TDS / Tracker Radar** and **Disconnect** — best fit and the only ones with owner data, but **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** [V]: "non-commercial" is ambiguous for Play distribution and forbids any future monetisation; DDG's TDS also needs a rule engine (64 % of entries are "ignore unless a rule matches").
- **HaGeZi**, **AdGuard** — GPLv3 data [V]; avoidable risk.
- **Steven Black** — MIT covers only his additions; upstreams include NC licences [V].
- **Peter Lowe** — no explicit licence [V]; only with written permission, not pursued now.
- **1Hosts** — MPL-2.0 but 779 KB gz, over budget.

## R2 — Owner (entity) grouping for first party

**Decision**: **No owner data.** First party = same **registrable domain** (FR-008's conditional clause does not apply because the chosen source has no owner data).

**Rationale**: Only the NC-licensed lists carry owner data. A hand-written owner map would be guesswork that silently unblocks trackers. Consequence: `doubleclick.net` on `youtube.com` is blocked (desired).

## R3 — Registrable domain: Public Suffix List

**Decision**: Bundle the full **Public Suffix List** (`public_suffix_list.dat`, ICANN + private sections, 10,336 rules, **≈90 KB gzip**) and a small pure-Kotlin matcher (normal, wildcard `*.` and exception `!` rules). Cache results in a bounded map (host → registrable domain).

**Rationale**: No public Android/androidx API computes eTLD+1 [assumption, from knowledge; none found]. OkHttp's `topPrivateDomain()` would add a dependency for one function (§IX, YAGNI). The private section is needed so `alice.github.io` and `bob.github.io` are different sites. Licence **MPL-2.0** [V]: keep the file's header, state its source; the app's code is unaffected.

**Edge rules**: IP literals and single-label hosts are their own site; a host that *is* a public suffix is its own site.

**Never-block set**: a short hand-written list of content and sign-in hosts (`accounts.google.com`, `appleid.apple.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `youtube.com`, `youtube-nocookie.com`, `googlevideo.com`, `ytimg.com`, `maps.googleapis.com`, `gstatic.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`, `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`), checked before the tracker set, guards FR-004a against future list refreshes.

## R4 — Blocking requests in WebView

**Decision**: `BrowserWebViewClient.shouldInterceptRequest(view, request)`:
- `request.isForMainFrame` → record the top-level URL for this WebView (an `AtomicReference`, because the callback runs on a WebView IO thread [D]) and return `null`.
- otherwise, if protection applies to the top site and the request host is a listed tracker of a *different* registrable domain and not on the never-block set → return an **empty `WebResourceResponse`** (`text/plain`, status 403, reason "Blocked", empty stream) and add the host to the page's blocked set; else `null`.
- Subresource HTTP errors with our status are already ignored: `onReceivedHttpError` only reports the main frame today (codebase map), so no error UI appears (FR-007).

**Facts**
- Sees iframes, images, scripts, CSS, fonts, media, XHR/fetch [D/B]; does **not** see WebSockets [B] or service-worker fetches [D].
- Service-worker requests go to the global `ServiceWorkerControllerCompat` client, which has **no top-frame context**, so FR-004's third-party test cannot be applied. **Not intercepted** in this spec — documented limitation, with WebSockets.
- Top frame is also refreshed from `onPageStarted` and `doUpdateVisitedHistory` (UI thread) to cover history/back-forward restores that issue no main-frame request [B]; where `WebViewFeature.NAVIGATION_LISTENER` is supported [V], `onNavigationCompleted` is used instead.
- Race: late subresources of the previous page may be judged against the new page's site — at worst one request mis-classified [B]; acceptable.
- Lookup cost: host + parent suffixes against a `HashSet<String>` (≤ ~6 probes) plus a cached registrable-domain lookup — microseconds, no I/O, no locks on the hot path.

## R5 — Global Privacy Control

**Decision**:
- When `WebViewFeature.MULTI_PROFILE` **and** `CUSTOM_REQUEST_HEADERS` are supported [V], call once per process `WebViewCompat.getProfile(webView).addCustomHeader(CustomHeader("Sec-GPC", "1", setOf("*")))`. The header then goes on **all** requests including subresources, prefetch and service-worker requests, not WebSockets [V, KDoc]. Incognito shares the default profile in this app, so it is covered. `"*"` as an origin rule is [B] — confirm on device; fallback rule set: `setOf("https://*", "http://*")` if the format rejects a bare `*`.
- Otherwise (older WebView, e.g. API 24 AVD's WebView 53), pass `mapOf("Sec-GPC" to "1")` to every `loadUrl` the app issues. Links a page opens itself are not covered (re-issuing every link click would break POST, activation and pop-up semantics) — spec FR-030 amended.
- `navigator.globalPrivacyControl` is not exposed by WebView [B] and would need an injected script — out of scope (FR-031, Spec 024).

## R6 — Referrer trimming

**Decision**: Rely on Chromium's default `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` (since M85 [B]), never loosen it, and make every app re-issued navigation send **no** referrer (plain `loadUrl` sends none [B]).

**Rationale**: `androidx.webkit` 1.17.0 has no referrer-policy API (grep of all sources) [V]; a profile-wide custom `Referer` would be one static value. A page that sets `Referrer-Policy: unsafe-url` cannot be overridden — spec FR-028/FR-029 amended to say so.

## R7 — HTTPS upgrade

**Decision**: One pure decision function and two choke points.
- `prepareNavigation(url, isIncognito)` (strip parameters, then upgrade) runs **before every `loadUrl` the app issues** — the `actions.loadUrl` lambda and the initial-load path in `BrowserWebView` are the only call sites (codebase map), so typed addresses, Home search, bookmarks, history, Spec 020 intents and tab switches all pass through it.
- `shouldOverrideUrlLoading(view, request)` for main-frame GET navigations started by the page: if `prepareNavigation` returns a different URL, `loadUrl(prepared)` and return `true`. Never re-issue the same URL (avoid loop [D]). Same-document changes are skipped.
- Upgrade only when: scheme `http`; host not `localhost`, not an IP literal, not single-label; site not excepted; host not in the session's failed set.
- **Failure detection** for the pending upgrade (host + original URL held per WebView):
  - `onReceivedError` with `isForMainFrame` and the pending https URL → fallback;
  - `onReceivedSslError` (already always `cancel()`s) with `error.url` matching the pending URL → fallback;
  - `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` with `isRedirect` to `http://` on the same host → allow it (return `false`), record failure, no loop.
  - Fallback = add host to the in-memory failed set, `loadUrl(originalHttp)`, and **do not** report `onLoadFailed` (no error UI).
- A secure attempt that returns any HTTP status (including 404) is the site's answer (FR-021): `onReceivedHttpError` is not a failure signal.
- **Back stack** [B]: calling `loadUrl` from `onReceivedError` before the error page commits should leave no entry; if a gate shows a leftover entry, the experimental `WebViewCompat.navigate(… setShouldReplaceCurrentEntry(true))` [V, `@ExperimentalNavigate`] is *not* adopted (experimental) — the limitation is recorded instead.
- POST navigations are not seen by `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` [D] and are never upgraded or stripped; no own timeout timer (a slow valid HTTPS site must not be downgraded).

**Failed-host memory**: `@Singleton` in-memory set, process lifetime, never persisted (FR-020).

## R8 — Tracking-parameter list

**Decision**: **Write our own list** of ~45 parameter names and prefixes in `assets/protection/tracking_params.txt` (prefix entries end with `*`, e.g. `utm_*`). Parameter names are facts; a hand-picked list carries no licence obligation [assumption, low risk]. Seed list: `utm_*`, `gclid`, `gclsrc`, `dclid`, `gbraid`, `wbraid`, `_ga`, `_gl`, `fbclid`, `fb_action_ids`, `fb_action_types`, `fb_source`, `fb_ref`, `msclkid`, `twclid`, `ttclid`, `li_fat_id`, `igshid`, `yclid`, `ysclid`, `epik`, `rdt_cid`, `sccid`, `irclickid`, `mc_cid`, `mc_eid`, `_hsenc`, `_hsmi`, `__hssc`, `__hstc`, `__hsfp`, `hsCtaTracking`, `mkt_tok`, `oly_anon_id`, `oly_enc_id`, `vero_id`, `wickedid`, `s_cid`, `ck_subscriber_id`. Generic names (`ref`, `source`, `cid`) are excluded because they break sites.

Rejected: ClearURLs (LGPL-3.0, 106 KB), AdGuard URL filter (GPLv3), DuckDuckGo's 25-entry list (Apache-2.0, fine but smaller than ours).

**Stripping rules**: exact, case-sensitive name match (or prefix for `*` entries); keep order, values and fragment; drop an emptied `?`; operate on the raw query string so encodings of kept parameters are byte-identical.

## R9 — Size budget

| Asset | gzip (≈ APK delta) |
|---|---|
| `tracker_hosts.txt` | ≈ 108 KB |
| `public_suffix_list.dat` | ≈ 90 KB |
| `tracking_params.txt` | < 1 KB |
| Code + strings (estimate from 021/022) | ≈ 60–90 KB |
| **Total** | **≈ 260–290 KB ≤ 500 KB (SC-010)** |

Assets are stored compressed in the APK (no `noCompress` entry for `.txt`/`.dat`).

## R10 — Loading the lists without slowing start-up

**Decision**: A `@Singleton` `ProtectionDataSource` parses the three assets on `Dispatchers.IO` into immutable sets, **started from `ThirtySixApplication.onCreate` without waiting** (like the Spec 014 retention sweep). `shouldInterceptRequest` is already on a background thread: if a request arrives before parsing finishes, it **waits** on the load (bounded by `NetworkTimeouts.PROTECTION_DATA_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`, failing open on timeout) — the first page load is the only one that can wait, and parsing ≈26k lines is expected in tens of ms [B, measure in G-perf]. The main thread never waits: main-thread callers (the app's `loadUrl` sites) use a non-blocking `matchersOrNull()`, and when it is not ready yet (a cold start straight into a link) they await on IO in a coroutine before loading; `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` skips rewriting when not ready (analyze I1). Heap: ≈16k host strings + PSL rules, estimated 2–3 MB [B, measure].

## R11 — Per-site exceptions storage

**Decision**: Room **v3 → v4**, additive `MIGRATION_3_4` creating `site_protection_exceptions(site TEXT PRIMARY KEY, added_at INTEGER NOT NULL)`, mirroring Spec 021's `site_permissions`. `site` is the registrable domain. A `@Singleton` cache collects the table into a `StateFlow<Set<String>>` so the IO-thread intercept path reads a snapshot without touching Room. Incognito exceptions live in an in-memory `@Singleton` store cleared on the incognito 1 → 0 transition in `IncognitoTabRepositoryImpl` (where the cookie snapshot is already restored).

Rejected: DataStore string-set (no observe-and-list ergonomics, no "added at"); persisting incognito exceptions with a flag (violates FR-014).

## R12 — Blocked count on the hub without recomposing the chrome

**Decision**: Each page's blocked hosts go into a concurrent set owned by a per-WebView `PageProtectionMonitor`; it publishes a separate `StateFlow<PageProtectionStatus>` (count, protection on/off, connection secure) conflated so bursts collapse. Only the hub reads it (§V rule 3: high-frequency state isolated from `BrowserUiState`). Reset and the per-page `protectionOn` happen in `onMainFrameRequest` on the IO thread, which runs before any of the new page's resources; `PageSession.advance()` only updates UI-facing fields and covers restores that issue no main-frame request (analyze U1). Same-document changes reset nothing.

## R13 — Clear browsing data and About

- New `ClearBrowsingDataCategory.SitesWithoutProtection`, excluded from `DEFAULT_SELECTION` (opt-in, like `SitePermissions`); clears Room exceptions **and** the incognito store.
- `AboutSection` gains an **Open-source notices** block (EasyList/EasyPrivacy CC BY-SA 3.0, Public Suffix List MPL-2.0), translated sentence with untranslated licence names and URLs. Licence texts ship in `assets/licenses/` and the repo.

## R14 — Testing approach

- **Unit (JVM)**: PSL matcher (normal/wildcard/exception, IPs, single-label, private section); tracker matcher (suffix match, first-party, never-block); parameter stripper (SC-004's 10 cases); upgrade eligibility and failed-set; prepareNavigation composition; exceptions repository and incognito store; `MIGRATION_3_4` test (real Room builder pattern from Spec 015); clear-data branch; ViewModel/hub state.
- **Instrumented**: blocked hosts need no DNS — a fake list (Hilt test module) containing `tracker-a.test` … lets a local fixture page (served by `AssetPageServer`) reference 12 `*.test` tracker hosts that are refused before any lookup, plus unlisted resources from the local server (SC-001, SC-011). HTTPS fallback via a local HTTP-only server. GPC via a header-echo fixture.
- **Device gates**: SC-002 (10 real sites), SC-003 (real http sites), SC-005 (page load on/off), SC-006 (cold start), SC-012 (proxy capture — `adb emu network capture` records nothing on these AVDs, Spec 022 note).
